output.reason: Sudden, painless, persistent monocular vision loss two hours ago is a possible central retinal artery occlusion or retinal detachment, a stroke-equivalent/time-critical threat requiring immediate emergency assessment with eye imaging and specialist care.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Sudden painless loss of vision in one eye that hasn't returned can be a blocked retinal artery — a stroke-equivalent — or a retinal detachment, and treatment is time-critical. Do not drive yourself; have someone take you or call 911. If you develop face, arm or leg weakness, or trouble speaking, call 911 immediately.
differential: Central retinal artery occlusion (retinal stroke equivalent)
